Confirm that a 403 forbidden error is returned and that the operation is recorded in the audit logs as an unauthorized access attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for an unauthorized update attempt.
Register a moderator for an unauthorized update attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft deletion of a rule log entry by an admin. First, create and login as admin, create a rule log, then invoke the DELETE endpoint with the relevant ruleLogId. Check that the deleted_at timestamp is set, the record is excluded from standard queries, and that the operation is audit-logged. This tests lifecycle management and retention policies for rule logs.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for authentication.
Create a rule log entry to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion failure for a non-existent or already soft-deleted ruleLogId. Attempt to delete a rule log using a random UUID or an ID of a previously deleted rule log as admin, verifying that a 404 not found error is returned and that the audit trail is complete. No data should be affected in these situations.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account to attempt the deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test the successful search and pagination of external authentication logs by an admin. Register and login as admin, create several external auth log records with varying fields and error statuses, then call the PATCH endpoint with filters (e.g., by auth channel, status, or date range) and pagination parameters. Verify that the returned data matches the filters, supports correct pagination, and that sensitive authentication data is only visible to admins.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for auth context.
Create multiple external auth logs for search and filter coverage.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when providing invalid filter parameters to the external auth logs search API. As an admin, attempt to search using syntactically invalid or unsupported filter criteria and verify that the API returns descriptive validation errors, does not return or leak log data, and audit logs the failed search attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for authentication context.

scenarios.draft: Test the successful creation of a new sub-category under a valid parent category. First, create a parent category as an admin to ensure the parent exists. Then, create a sub-category with unique name and valid required fields (enabled, display_order, version, description, icon_uri). Confirm the returned sub-category has correct hierarchy and all schema fields, and that it is correctly linked to the parent. Audit fields should be populated and no errors should occur.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent category as prerequisite. The sub-category creation requires an existing parent category to link to.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to create a sub-category under a parent with a name already used by an existing (non-deleted) sub-category. Begin by creating a parent category and a first sub-category with a given name. Then, attempt to create a second sub-category under the same parent with the same name. The API should reject the request with a uniqueness or conflict error. Confirm error response semantics per business rule.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent category for sub-category containment.
Create a first sub-category with a specific name, setting up the uniqueness constraint conflict.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of a sub-category's editable fields by an admin. Set up by creating a parent category and a sub-category, then update properties like name, description, display_order, enabled status, and icon_uri. Validate the updated fields persist and audit/versioning fields are changed. The sub-category's parent linkage should remain intact and the operation must not introduce cycles.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent category for sub-category linkage.
Create an initial sub-category as update target.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to update a sub-category's name to one already in use (and not deleted) under the same parent. Create a parent and two sibling sub-categories with unique names, then attempt to update the second sub-category's name to that of the first. The API should reject this with a validation or conflict error. Confirm the error message and that the original value is unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create parent category.
Create two sibling sub-categories with unique names so the test can attempt to violate uniqueness.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft deletion of a sub-category by an admin. Create a parent category and sub-category, then execute the delete operation. Confirm the sub-category's deleted_at field is set, it is no longer listed in subcategory lists, but data remains for audit. Attempt to fetch the deleted sub-category and expect not found or deleted status.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent category as prerequisite.
Create sub-category to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to delete a sub-category that is in use (either as parent of another sub-category or assigned to posts). Create a parent category, then create a sub-category, then either create a post assigned to this sub-category or a child sub-category. Attempt to delete the in-use sub-category; confirm API rejects deletion with a clear usage dependency error and returns appropriate status.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent category for hierarchy setup.
Create the sub-category which will later be referenced.
Create a child sub-category to establish a dependency preventing delete, or alternatively, create a post referencing the sub-category.

scenarios.draft: Test correct filtering and pagination of policy document search. Create several policy documents with various fields (title, version, status, content). Search using filters on title, activity status, and content, and test pagination with limit/offset or cursor parameters. Confirm response structure matches schema, results match applied filters, and respect pagination boundaries.

dependencies.purpose: Create several policy documents to establish search/test dataset.

scenarios.draft: Test search on policy documents with filters that do not match any records. Confirm that an empty result set is returned, and response indicates zero items but no error. Pagination metadata should reflect no results. This verifies correct handling of no-match scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure dataset is present so filter-out can be tested meaningfully.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a single policy document by valid ID. Create a new policy document as admin, then retrieve it by its returned UUID. Confirm full schema fields (title, body, version, author, timestamps, status) are present and correct. Validate correct status/visibility for different document states.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new policy document to retrieve and verify by ID.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval attempt with a non-existent or soft-deleted policy documentId. Attempt to fetch a random (or deleted) UUID, verify API returns a clear not found error and does not leak any document data. This tests correct error reporting and access control.

Test successful soft-deletion of a post report by a moderator. A moderator, after being authenticated, selects an existing post report (which is in a terminal state such as 'resolved' or 'closed') and performs a DELETE operation. The test should verify that the post report is soft-deleted (deleted_at set), the corresponding audit logs are updated, and the report is removed from subsequent report searches. Dependency: Needs a post report to exist and be resolvable by the moderator.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new discussion post so that it can be reported.
Member reports the newly created post to generate a post report for moderation.
Moderator resolves or closes the report before deletion to simulate its end-of-life state.

scenarios.draft: Test failure case when a moderator attempts to delete a post report with a non-existent or already deleted postReportId. The system should return a clear 'not found' error and no action is taken on any resource. This validates error reporting and idempotency of deletion requests.

Test that an unauthorized user or insufficiently privileged role cannot invoke the moderator DELETE post report endpoint. Attempt to call this endpoint with a member, guest, or unauthenticated session and verify 'forbidden' error is thrown and no audit data is changed.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member for use in the unauthorized role test.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can search and paginate comment reports with various filters and sort/pagination parameters. Create multiple comment abuse reports with different statuses, reporters, types, and time windows. Use the search endpoint to paginate, filter by status/type/date, and assert correct inclusion/exclusion of records. Also test edge cases like empty results when using overly restrictive filters. Validate all audit and summary fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create discussion posts to enable commenting.
Add comments to posts so they may be reported.
File multiple abuse reports on different comments to seed test data.

scenarios.draft: Test that users without admin or moderator privileges (guests, members) are forbidden from searching comment reports using this admin endpoint. Attempt access as a member and as a guest, and verify that the access is denied with a proper forbidden error message. Confirm that no records are returned or leaked.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account to use in unauthorized access test.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve and paginate the set of comment reports, filtering by status, reporter, report type, and time window. Prepare several comments with abuse reports in different states. Use PATCH with various filters to verify correct data inclusion, empty results for restrictive filters, and proper pagination controls. Confirm moderator visibility matches admin's, except for permission differences.

dependencies.purpose: Create posts for comment and abuse paths.
Add comments to posts to be reported.
Create reports on comments in different states for filtering.

scenarios.draft: Test that search attempts on the moderator comment report endpoint by non-moderator roles (member, guest) are rejected with a forbidden error. No results should be returned and no partial matches are permitted.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member for use in unauthorized test.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a specific comment report's full details by an admin. Create a comment, report it for abuse, then retrieve the report by its unique ID using the GET endpoint. Verify all relevant fields are present, statuses reflect report state, and included audit/comment/message fields are consistent with those created.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to enable commenting.
Add a comment to the post to be reported.
File an abuse report on the comment to obtain a valid commentReportId.

scenarios.draft: Test the error condition when an admin attempts to GET a comment report by a non-existent or deleted commentReportId. The system should return a clear not found error message, and no sensitive information should be disclosed.

Test that an unauthorized user (e.g., regular member or guest) cannot access the admin GET comment report endpoint. Attempt to use this endpoint without admin or moderator privileges and confirm a forbidden or unauthorized error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register a test member for the unauthorized access path.

scenarios.draft: Test a moderator's ability to retrieve a specific comment report by its unique ID. Set up by creating a comment, reporting it, then using the moderator GET endpoint to fetch details. Validate the returned report includes all expected fields and audit data, and is visible to the moderator role.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for commenting and abuse flow.
Create a comment as a target for the abuse report.
Report the comment as abusive to get a commentReportId.

scenarios.draft: Test the GET comment report by moderator returns not found error when given a non-existent or deleted commentReportId. No sensitive or audit data should be exposed on error.

Test that users without moderator or admin role cannot retrieve comment report details from the moderator endpoint. Attempt access as a member or guest and validate access denial and no data leakage occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account for testing lack of sufficient permissions.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new user metrics analytic profile for a discussion board member. Precondition: a member account exists (created via the member registration endpoint). The admin creates a user metrics profile for that member, initializing all analytic counters such as posts, comments, votes, reports, and reputation. The scenario validates that all counters initialize correctly and that duplicate creation attempts are blocked by the system. Audit logs are verified for tracking the creation event.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new discussion board member to obtain a valid memberId necessary for metrics profile creation.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an existing user metrics analytic record with new activity counters (e.g., posts, comments, votes), reputation value, or participation statistics. Ensure that only allowable fields are changed, and audit logs reflect the update. Precondition is that a user metrics record exists for an active member. Attempting to update immutable reference fields such as user reference should be rejected, and invalid or negative counter values should return validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user metrics profile for a specific member to serve as the target for update testing.

scenarios.draft: Test successful hard deletion of a user metrics analytic record by a system admin. Precondition is an existing user metrics record for a member. Validate that after deletion, the metric cannot be retrieved or re-created, and that the deletion event is properly audit-logged. Test error handling by attempting to delete a non-existent or already deleted user metrics entity; expect a not found error response in those cases.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user metrics analytic profile to ensure there is an existing record for deletion testing.

scenarios.draft: Test paginated and filtered search retrieval of daily statistics records. Provide various filter combinations such as date range, metric thresholds, and sort orders, verifying that the result set matches the filters. The scenario should validate pagination mechanics with different page sizes and verifies that invalid or out-of-bound search criteria return clear error messages. All result records must exclude detailed content info for privacy.

Test fetching a single day's summary statistics record by its unique dailyStatsId. Verify that the endpoint returns the correct aggregate values and all expected KPIs, and that requesting a non-existent or deleted dailyStatsId returns a not found error. Also validate that only admin roles can access this endpoint and audit compliance is observed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a daily statistics record and capture its dailyStatsId to be fetched in the get-by-id scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that an authenticated member can search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of discussion board posts. Verify filters for title, body, category, specific time windows, and pagination parameters. Ensure only posts with status 'active' or 'visible' are returned to members (hidden, flagged, or deleted posts should be excluded by default). Validate that the results respect the specified page size and offset. Check edge scenarios like empty filters, out-of-range pagination, or invalid filter fields resulting in graceful errors or empty result sets.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new discussion board member to authenticate and receive a JWT for accessing member APIs.
Obtain a valid JWT session for the member to use in searching posts.
Create several posts in various categories and with various statuses to serve as search/filter targets in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that a non-authenticated user or a user without a valid member role cannot access this API to search for member-only posts. Attempt to call the endpoint with an invalid or missing token and verify that an appropriate forbidden/unauthorized error is returned. This ensures role-based access control is correctly enforced for member-specific post searches.

dependencies.purpose: Provision sample post data for search context.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can search and retrieve discussion board posts including drafts, hidden, flagged, and deleted posts, as well as active posts. Verify advanced filters for category, status, author role, and rich search (e.g., by title, keyword, or body content). Ensure that moderator role allows access to posts that are not visible to regular members. Paginate results and validate correct total counts, especially when filtering by post status or category.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a moderator user to receive appropriate permissions and JWT access.
Log in as the moderator to obtain a valid JWT for the search.
Create posts with various statuses (draft, flagged, hidden, deleted) to act as search and filter targets.

scenarios.draft: Test the API by providing invalid filter fields or values as a moderator, and verify that the system returns informative errors for unsupported search criteria or out-of-bounds pagination parameters. Additionally, ensure that users lacking moderator role (such as regular members or unauthenticated clients) receive appropriate forbidden errors when attempting to access this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create a standard member account to attempt a forbidden API call and ensure correct security enforcement.
Obtain a member JWT token to try the API for forbidden access.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can search all posts across the discussion board, including hidden, flagged, deleted, and active posts. Check search flexibility with filters for post status, author, category, and free text across title/body. Results must include audit metadata visible only to admins when returned. Confirm pagination correctness and robustness with large result sets and complex queries. Validate system behavior on invalid filters and possible edge cases (empty result, invalid category, negative page indexes).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account and receive access.
Admin login to retrieve the necessary JWT for privileged access.
Create a variety of posts under different statuses and categories to robustly test the search and filter functionality as an admin.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that only users with the admin role can access the admin search endpoint. Attempt access with moderator role, member role, and unauthenticated session. Confirm that the system returns forbidden errors and does not leak privileged post data to unauthorized users.

dependencies.purpose: Establish a moderator account to test forbidden access to admin-only endpoint.
Set up a member account to try access for permission enforcement.

scenarios.draft: Test that an authenticated member can retrieve all details of a single, existing, and active post by postId. The response should include author profile, category info, entire title, body, and attachments. Ensure correct behavior for posts created by self or others. Confirm that only posts with 'active' status and not soft-deleted are accessible and that the result includes all expected fields for full detail view.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to act as the reader.
Log in to obtain the JWT for accessing post details.
Create a post with status 'active' for retrieval by postId.

scenarios.draft: Test attempts to retrieve a post as a member where the post is either hidden, flagged, deleted (soft-deleted), or does not exist. Ensure that hidden or flagged posts are not accessible by regular members and appropriate errors (not found or forbidden) are returned. Also attempt to fetch using a random, non-existent postId to confirm that a clear 404 not found error is produced.

dependencies.purpose: Create and log in as a member for the test context.
Create a post with non-active (hidden/flagged/deleted) status as a moderator.

scenarios.draft: Verify that non-authenticated users or those with invalid JWT tokens cannot retrieve member-specific posts by postId. Attempt to call with a guest role or expired/invalid JWT and expect a forbidden error, ensuring API security and access restriction to members only.

dependencies.purpose: Obtain a guest JWT to try unauthorized access.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can access the detailed view of any post by postId, regardless of the post's status (active, hidden, flagged, or soft-deleted). Check that audit and moderation metadata (such as moderation status, history, or flags) are included in the response for privileged roles, and all content fields are present. Verify error handling on invalid postIds or attempting access with a non-moderator role.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator account to perform the retrieval.
Log in as a moderator to obtain the JWT.
Create posts with various statuses to test moderator visibility for each type.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a permission matrix policy entry by its unique ID. First, create an admin account and log in to obtain an access token. Then, use the permission matrix creation endpoint to create a new RBAC/ACL policy entry, capturing its UUID for use in this scenario. Attempt to fetch the permission matrix by its ID and verify that the correct details are returned (role, resource, action, allowed, and audit fields).

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account that can access permission matrix APIs.
Authenticate the admin user to obtain a valid JWT for authorization.
Create a new permission matrix policy entry in order to have a valid ID to retrieve.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling for when a non-existent permission matrix ID is provided. After admin setup and authentication, attempt to retrieve a permission matrix using a random, non-existent UUID. Expect a 404 Not Found error response and a clear error message indicating the ID does not correspond to any record.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account that can access permission matrix APIs.
Authenticate the admin user to obtain a valid JWT for authorization.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new permission matrix entry. Create an admin user and log in to obtain authentication. Call the creation endpoint with valid role, resource, action, and allowed parameters. Verify the system creates the policy entry, returning all fields in the response and that the creation is auditable in the rule log.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user with permission to create a permission matrix entry.
Authenticate admin and obtain JWT.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to create a permission matrix policy entry that duplicates role/resource/action/effective_from combination. Setup: register admin, authenticate, create a permission matrix, then attempt to create another one with the exact same parameters. System must return a conflict or validation error, enforcing unique constraints as per schema and requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user with permission to create a permission matrix entry.
Authenticate admin and obtain JWT.
Create the first permission matrix with certain role/resource/action/effective_from values.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of an existing permission matrix. Register and authenticate as admin, create a permission matrix, then update allowed/action/resource fields for the created entry. Verify the changes are applied, returned in the response, and all audit fields are refreshed accordingly.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account.
Authenticate admin and obtain JWT.
Create the original permission matrix to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test that updating a non-existent or already deleted permission matrix returns an error. Register and authenticate admin, then attempt to update a random or previously deleted UUID. The system should return a clear error indicating the absence of the target entry.

dependencies.purpose: Admin setup.
Authenticate admin and obtain JWT.

scenarios.draft: Test soft deletion of a permission matrix entry. Register and authenticate admin, create a permission matrix, then soft-delete it using this endpoint. Confirm that the permission matrix record's deleted_at field is set, the matrix is excluded from future list/search requests, and attempts to use the ID in 'get' or 'update' return a not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account.
Authenticate admin and obtain JWT.
Create a permission matrix entry to be soft-deleted.

scenarios.draft: Test idempotency and error handling for deleting a non-existent or already soft-deleted permission matrix. Attempt to delete the same permissionMatrixId twice or use a random UUID that doesn't correspond to a real entry. The system should handle repeated attempts gracefully, returning appropriate errors or idempotent responses.

dependencies.purpose: Admin setup.
Admin authentication.

scenarios.draft: Test successful paginated, filtered search over rule log entries. Register and authenticate as admin, ensure at least one rule change log exists by creating or updating a permission matrix. Then, perform a search/filter query using this endpoint and check for consistent pagination, returned data, and correct field mapping. Validate that searching by operator, rule type, or time range works as described.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account with access to rule logs.
Authenticate as admin.
Create or update a permission matrix to ensure a rule log entry exists.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when the filter conditions result in no rule log records, or if an invalid filter/syntax is provided. Register and authenticate as admin. Attempt to search with a filter guaranteed to return no records (e.g., use a far future date range or a non-existent operator id) and expect an empty page or clear not found response. Also, input invalid filter syntax and verify the system returns validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account.
Authenticate as admin.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft-deletion of an existing comment report by admin. First, create a new comment report as a member to ensure a valid commentReportId. Then, as an admin, attempt to delete this report and verify the deleted_at field is set and the report is excluded from search results. Verify audit logs are updated for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new comment report as a member to have a valid commentReportId to delete.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to soft-delete a comment report using a non-existent or already deleted commentReportId. The system should return an appropriate not found error. This validates error handling for invalid targets and helps prevent data leaks or audit errors.

Test soft-delete of a comment report by a user without admin or moderator role. Attempt to call the endpoint as a member or guest; system must reject the action with a forbidden error and log the attempt for audit.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new comment report as a member to obtain a valid commentReportId.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft-deletion of an existing comment report by moderator. Create a report as a member, then, using moderator role, delete the report and ensure it is removed from search results, and the deleted_at field is set correctly. Moderation audit trail should be verified.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment report to produce a valid commentReportId for moderator deletion.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to soft-delete a comment report with a non-existent or already deleted commentReportId as moderator. The API should return a not found error, confirming robust error handling for moderation actions.

Test soft-deletion of a comment report by a user who is not a moderator. Use a member role to attempt the action, expect a forbidden error, and verify no records are deleted or altered. Confirm audit logging of unauthorized attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid comment report to attempt unauthorized deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of user sanction records as admin for compliance review. Create one or more sanction records, then use different search filters (by status, type, or user) and confirm pagination, filtering, and expected data structure. Ensure sensitive and summary info is returned accurately, and only active (non-deleted) records appear.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one sanction record to validate search, pagination, and filtering features.

scenarios.draft: Test searching for user sanctions with a filter that matches no records (e.g., non-existent userId or status). Validate that the system returns an empty result page, proper pagination metadata, and no error. This ensures correct UX for non-match queries.

Test user sanction search access control by attempting to call as a non-admin (e.g., member or guest). System must deny access and return a forbidden error, verifying strict authorization enforcement.

Test a moderator successfully retrieving a paginated, filtered list of user sanction records for moderation/audit. Ensure that returned entries match filter criteria, support pagination, and omit sensitive fields as appropriate. Test using a sanction record created for this purpose.

dependencies.purpose: Create a sanction record under a member to verify search and pagination as moderator.

scenarios.draft: Search user sanctions as moderator with filters that do not match any records. Ensure the API returns an empty array with correct pagination structure and no errors, confirming robustness in result handling.

Attempt user sanction search as a non-privileged user (member or guest), expecting a permission denied error. This scenario checks that only admin and moderator roles are authorized to access sensitive sanction records.

Test successful retrieval of a full user sanction record by ID as admin. After creating a user sanction, fetch its details and confirm all fields, including audit, sanction reason, and status. This scenario verifies correct linkage and data visibility for compliance reviews.

dependencies.purpose: Create a sanction record to obtain a valid userSanctionId for detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to retrieve a user sanction with a non-existent or already deleted userSanctionId as admin, ensuring the system returns a not found error and no private or audit details are leaked.

Attempt to retrieve a user sanction as a user without admin or moderator role (e.g., as a member or guest). Confirm access is denied and no record details are returned, ensuring strict RBAC and sensitive information is protected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a sanction record so a non-privileged test can attempt unauthorized access to a real record.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a comment on a discussion board post by a moderator. First, ensure a moderator account and an active post exist. Authenticate as the moderator, then submit a new comment with valid content (within the schema field length constraint). Expect a successful creation, with returned comment containing all expected schema fields and relationships (post linkage, moderator as author, timestamps). Verify audit fields and the association with the correct post.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate a new moderator to serve as the comment author.
Create a discussion post as the target for the comment, performed as the moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to create a comment with invalid input fails. Using a valid moderator session and an existing post, attempt comment creation with invalid data (e.g., exceeding maximum body length, or missing required fields). The API should reject the request with detailed validation errors. Confirm no comment is created and that error messages match schema constraint violations.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator to authenticate as comment author.
Create a valid discussion post to enable comment attempts.

scenarios.draft: Test that comment creation fails when the target post does not exist. Authenticate as a moderator, and attempt to create a comment using a randomly generated or deleted/nonexistent postId. The API must return a not found or forbidden error, and no comment should be created.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator and obtain authentication for test context.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a comment on a discussion board post by an admin. First, ensure an admin user and an active post exist. Authenticate as the admin, then submit a valid comment associated with the post. The response should return the created comment object with appropriate audit fields, post linkage, author (admin), timestamps, and other schema-defined data.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account to perform comment creation.
Create a discussion post as the admin, providing a valid postId for comment linkage.

scenarios.draft: Verify that duplicate comment submissions (e.g., accidental double-submit with same payload) do not create duplicate records or have side effects. As an admin, create a post, then submit the same comment twice in rapid succession. The system should enforce idempotency or return a duplicate error, and only one comment instance should be created.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to author comments.
Create a target post for comment submission.

scenarios.draft: Verify that creating a comment on a soft-deleted post as an admin is forbidden. First, create and then soft-delete a post. Attempt to create a comment on the deleted post and expect an error (not found or forbidden), with proper error reporting. No comment should be created in this scenario.

dependencies.purpose: Admin creation and authentication for comment author context.
Create a new post to serve as comment target.
Soft-delete the post before attempting comment creation to simulate the error scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member can successfully update their own comment within allowed edit windows. Register a member, create a post, submit a comment, then update the comment's body field (with valid new content) before edit lock time expires. Expect the API to return the updated comment object, reflect changed content, updated timestamps, and correct audit fields. The comment's parent, author, and linkage remain unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a member who will author the comment.
Create a post for the comment to be associated with.
Create the original comment by the member prior to update.

dependencies.purpose: Register member for authoring the comment.

dependencies.purpose: Create moderator to authenticate update requests.
Establish a post for comment hosting.

dependencies.purpose: Moderator registration for authentication context.
Create a post for the test (a comment will not exist yet for random commentId).

scenarios.draft: Verify an admin can update any comment, regardless of author or edit window policy. Register an admin, create a post, add a comment as a member/mod/admin, then update the comment via the admin-authorized endpoint. The comment's data, timestamps, and audit fields should reflect the update. Admin privilege allows override of standard restrictions.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate an admin user to carry out comment updates.

Add a comment to the post prior to admin update.

scenarios.draft: Test that invalid update attempts by admin (such as setting read-only/audit fields or passing illegal values) are rejected. dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for authoring the update.
Create a post and establish a comment for the update test.
Prepare a comment for illegal update attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to update a soft-deleted comment via the admin API returns a not found or forbidden error. First, create a comment and then soft-delete it. Attempt to update the deleted comment as an admin and verify the error response and lack of modification.

dependencies.purpose: Admin authentication needed for update request.
Create a post for use in this workflow.
Create a comment for subsequent deletion.
Soft-delete the comment prior to update, simulating logical removal.

Validate the response for a not-found error. This checks that repeated deletions or references to missing sanctions are handled gracefully, as required for robust admin workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate an admin to permit sanction deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when a non-admin (member, moderator, guest) tries to call DELETE /discussionBoard/admin/userSanctions/{userSanctionId}. Register as member and moderator, and attempt the delete as each non-admin user for an existing sanction. Verify forbidden error responses and audit log updates, confirming that only admins may delete sanction records and that access control is enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create admin to register other accounts and to create sanction record.
Register member for unauthorized test and as sanction target.
Register moderator for unauthorized test.
Admin creates a sanction for the member, so the member/moderator can attempt to delete it (should not succeed).

This verifies privilege boundaries and moderation flow.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a moderator for access.

dependencies.purpose: To register and authenticate the moderator for searching notifications.

scenarios.draft: Test forbidden access when a user with a non-moderator role (admin, member, guest) attempts PATCH /discussionBoard/moderator/notifications. dependencies.purpose: To register and authenticate users for role-based access tests.
Member account for negative (forbidden) test case.

dependencies.purpose: Register member and obtain access token for notification search context.

scenarios.draft: Test notification search result returns empty page when there are no notifications for the member or the filter is unmatched. Ensures that the endpoint's response is robust to zero-record cases and UI can react accordingly.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member account for a guaranteed empty-inbox scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting PATCH /discussionBoard/member/notifications from a non-member role (admin, moderator, guest) returns forbidden. Attempt this action with admin and moderator authentication, and verify the forbidden response is provided and event is audit-logged.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for negative test of member endpoint access.
Moderator registration for negative test case.

Expect the report to be stored, notifications triggered for moderators/admins, and a correct response structure. Verify in the response that the report status is initially set to 'pending', and all audit fields are present.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member in order to obtain authentication credentials for reporting.

Add a comment to the post, setting up the target for the abuse report.

scenarios.draft: Check that a member cannot submit more than one report for the same comment. Attempt to submit another report with the same member and same comment. The system must reject the duplicate report attempt, enforcing the one-report-per-member-per-comment rule, and return a well-formed error message indicating the violation.

dependencies.purpose: Register member for authentication.
Obtain JWT for comment/report action.
Create a post to comment on.
Submit a new comment as the basis for reporting.
Submit the initial report to trigger the duplication constraint.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the member.
Obtain JWT for creating and reporting comments.
Create a post to allow comment creation.
Create a comment for potential deletion and failed report attempt.
Delete the comment (if simulating a deleted comment report scenario).

scenarios.draft: As an admin, verify the ability to submit a report for a comment authored by any user (e.g., in cases of manual moderation or audit). Verify that the admin can specify any valid comment and that all necessary workflow and notification actions occur. Confirm that the new report record is stored correctly, with status set to 'pending,' and audit/admin attribution is accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to obtain the necessary permissions for privileged actions.

Confirm that the moderator can complete the workflow, the report is correctly recorded, and audit trails reflect moderator context. Check that status and trigger notification behaviors match expectations.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator to obtain role privileges.

Create a standard member for original content submissions.

Validate that changes are reflected in the report's state, audit logs are updated, and all field changes are persisted according to compliance requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Provision an admin account for review actions.

Submit the abuse report that will later be reviewed and updated.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a moderator can update the status or enter moderation action/resolution on a comment report within their access scope. Ensure that attempted updates on already resolved or deleted reports are rejected, changes are properly tracked in the audit fields, and business rules for resolution progression are followed.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator and get JWT for authorization.

Create a member for comment/post creation.
Authenticate as member to create post/comment.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new post report by a member to ensure a valid post report exists for retrieval by the moderator.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discussion post and obtain its ID for metric initialization.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a privileged operation log by authorized admin. An admin creates an operation log via the proper endpoint, then fetches its details by ID. dependencies.purpose: Create an operation log record so that a valid operationLogId is available for retrieval and to ensure valid admin context.

Admin attempts to fetch details for a UUID not associated with any log or for a log already deleted. Verifies correct error handling and audit policy.

Test unauthorized access to an operation log by a non-admin user. Attempt retrieval with a session that lacks admin privileges (e.g., member or moderator context), ensuring the system properly rejects the request with a forbidden/insufficient privilege error and records the audit event for compliance.

Test creating a new privileged operation log as an authorized admin. Provide valid audit details (actor, action, resource, timestamp, context) per schema. Ensures system resilience and uniqueness constraints.

Test that users without admin privileges (e.g., member or moderator) cannot create an operation log. Attempts with lower privileges must be rejected with a forbidden/insufficient privilege error, and the incident should be audit logged.

Test successful update of fields in an existing operation log entry by an authorized admin. Confirm changes are reflected, all updates fully audit-logged, and the record maintains traceability.

Test that non-admin actors are forbidden from updating operation log entries. Attempt update as a member or moderator and expect a forbidden/insufficient privilege response, with all attempts logged for auditing.

Test successful soft-deletion of an operation log entry as an admin. Create a new operation log, then execute a soft delete on its operationLogId. dependencies.purpose: Create an operation log entry for deletion testing.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to soft-delete a non-existent or already removed operation log. Expect a not-found error, validating error handling for missing or already-soft-deleted operationLogId values and preventing unintended system state changes.

Test soft-deletion request as a non-admin. Attempt log removal from a member or moderator session, expecting a forbidden/insufficient privilege response. All unauthorized delete attempts should be audit logged for compliance and forensic review.

Test successful advanced search and pagination over policy change logs by providing various combinations of filters (admin, namespace, date range, resource/field, sort order). The solution is to fully invoke the curried functions before applying .slice() (or if the innermost invocation already returns a string long enough, no slice is needed). This occurs because 'extra' variable is sometimes an empty object ({}) and sometimes contains error fields (e.g., { error_code: "ERR_OAUTH", error_message: "OAuth failed" }). scenario.draft: Test a moderator accessing their own assignment and status info via their moderatorId. Register and log in as moderator, extract their moderatorId. Try to fetch their own profile. Validate successful response and returned data. Attempt to fetch a different moderatorId (if any) and validate access is denied. Also, test behavior on soft-deleted or non-existent moderatorId and ensure error/forbidden responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate a moderator to obtain moderatorId and token.

scenario.draft: Test admin updating a moderator's status and assignment details via moderatorId. Admin should be able to change moderator's status (active, revoked, suspended), assignment or revocation timestamps, and notes. Start by registering both an admin and a moderator. Admin performs status changes, with each change verified via get (detail) endpoint. Attempt updates with insufficient privilege (non-admin) and ensure error is returned. Also, test update with invalid data (e.g. illogical status transition, missing fields) to ensure proper validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to authenticate and authorize moderator status update actions.
Register a moderator to obtain their moderatorId for update.

scenario.draft: Test a successful admin password change. First, register a new admin using a unique email and valid password, obtaining the necessary JWT via the registration endpoint. Then, authenticate as this admin and use the JWT to call the password change endpoint, supplying the correct current password and a new password that meets policy requirements. Verify the response confirms the update. Finally, attempt to log in with the new password to ensure the change was applied and the old password no longer works. This scenario validates the basic password update flow, strict authentication, and security handling around credential changes.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin and obtain a valid JWT token for authentication. This is a prerequisite for password change. The email used must be unique to avoid conflicts.
Authenticate the admin to obtain a new JWT for password change and to test login with the new password after the password is changed.

scenario.draft: Test failure when attempting to change the admin password using an incorrect current password. Register a new admin and authenticate to obtain the JWT. Attempt to change the password by providing an incorrect 'oldPassword' value. Verify that the endpoint returns a proper error code and message, and that the password is not changed. Then, verify login with the original password still succeeds. This scenario checks security against credential brute-forcing and error transparency.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin and obtain the JWT required for the password change attempt.
Login as admin to verify the original password remains valid after the failed change attempt.

scenario.draft: Test failure when the new password does not meet system policy (e.g., too short, missing required characters). Register a new admin, authenticate, and attempt to change the password by providing a valid current password but an invalid new password (e.g., '123'). The system should reject the change, returning a validation error and not changing the password. Attempting login with the new password should fail, while the old password should still work. This verifies validation enforcement on the new password field.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin and log in to obtain a JWT for the password change attempt.
Login as admin to confirm the password was not changed after the failed update.

scenario.draft: Test that the password change API cannot be called without valid admin authentication. Attempt to change a password using a missing, expired, or invalid JWT token. The system should return an unauthorized error and not process the request. This scenario validates access controls and session/auth context requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to define a valid account in the system, although no JWT will be provided in the change password call.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a specific external authentication log entry by its unique ID as an admin. Precondition is the existence of an external auth log record. Validate that all necessary fields (auth channel, user, timestamps, error info) are returned. Confirm that non-admin requests and requests for non-existent or deleted log IDs return correct error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new external authentication log entry to have a valid ID for retrieval tests.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a new external authentication log entry with valid data as an admin. Ensure all mandatory and optional fields (auth channel, user reference, status, error context, timestamps) are captured. Validate business constraints for event completeness, correct mapping to users, referential integrity, and audit logging. Also test error scenarios: missing required fields, invalid input formats, or attempt by non-admin roles.

Test updating details of an existing external authentication log entry by ID as an admin. Perform updates to metadata (such as correcting channel, user references, or error status). Ensure modifications are accepted when valid and rejected with proper errors for invalid data or unauthorized roles. Validate audit trail integrity and confirm all updates are reflected in the retrieved log entry. Test error handling for updates to non-existent or deleted log entries.

dependencies.purpose: Create the external authentication log entry to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deletion of an external authentication log entry by admin. Ensure the 'deleted_at' timestamp is set and the log is excluded from standard queries/searched lists. After deletion, validate that attempts to access, update, or delete the same log entry return not found or forbidden errors as appropriate. Confirm only admin users are able to perform this operation, and audit trails record the delete action.

dependencies.purpose: Create the log entry that will be soft-deleted by admin.

scenario.draft: Test searching and retrieving paginated, filtered lists of outgoing email logs as an admin. Use a variety of filters such as recipient, email type, status, date range, and ensure responses include only matching logs. Validate pagination, correct sort order, and handling of search criteria. Confirm that only admin role can access this endpoint. Error cases include unauthorized requests and malformed filter input. Confirm soft-deleted records are excluded from results.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more outgoing email log records to be available for search results.

scenario.draft: Test the ability of an authenticated member to change their password. Initially, register a new member account and authenticate to obtain a valid session. Attempt a password change with a correct old password and verify success and audit trail update. Subsequently, test with an incorrect old password to ensure the operation fails and an appropriate error is returned. Attempt edge cases such as using a weak new password or attempting while the member is suspended or withdrawn, verifying validation and permission errors, respectively. Ensure that all password hash updates conform to security policy.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to obtain legitimate credentials for password change scenarios.
Authenticate as the registered member to obtain a valid session/JWT required for password change.
Modify member status to suspended/withdrawn for negative case scenarios where password change should fail.

scenario.draft: Test the registration of a new moderator account by an admin, covering both the typical successful registration and failure due to duplicate email. Begin by authenticating as an admin. Attempt to register a new moderator with unique email and expected fields, verify a JWT is issued and audit logs record the assignment. Then, try to register another moderator with the same email and validate that a conflict error is returned due to the unique email constraint. Ensure all responses contain appropriate headers and audit data.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin to be eligible to create new moderator accounts.

scenario.draft: Test moderator authentication by logging in with valid credentials, verifying that a new JWT token is issued, and audit logs are updated. Attempt login with incorrect password, non-existent account, and for a moderator whose status is suspended or revoked; each should result in appropriate authentication errors. Validate that audit logs are updated for both successful and failed attempts (distinguishing between not-found, wrong password, and not-active status once moderator status editing is available).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator account to have valid credentials and test against possible status changes.

scenario.draft: Test proper moderator logout operation by performing a session login, calling the logout endpoint, and verifying token invalidation and that subsequent privileged calls using the same token are rejected. Confirm audit logs and status updates to reflect the logout event, observing that session management rules are enforced for stateless JWTs or server-blacklist if applicable.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator as prerequisite for authentication.
Login with the moderator account to obtain a valid session/JWT for logout and post-logout session invalidation testing.

scenario.draft: Test JWT token validation for moderators. Register and log in as a moderator to acquire a valid token, then call the validate endpoint to confirm token is active and moderator profile is returned. Test for expired and tampered tokens, and when the moderator account status has been set to 'revoked' or 'suspended', validate that token validation fails with accurate error detail. Confirm all such attempts are logged for security and audit purposes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator account to validate with a legitimate token.
Obtain a legitimate JWT for validation scenarios.
Update the moderator status to 'revoked' or 'suspended' to test token validation failure for non-active accounts.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can successfully retrieve the full details of a specific policy change log by its policyChangeLogId. Ensure that all audit fields, before/after values, change reason, and actor_admin_id are returned as expected. The scenario requires a policy change log to exist, so first create a new policy change log entry and then retrieve it using its ID.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy change log entry to ensure that a valid ID exists for retrieval testing.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval failure for a non-existent policy change log by supplying an invalid or deleted policyChangeLogId. The system should return a 404 not found error. This checks the endpoint's robustness for missing records.

Verify successful creation of a policy change log entry by an admin. Provide all necessary audit fields such as admin actor, namespace, resource, field, before/after value, and change reason. Ensure the created log can be subsequently retrieved. If the API requires related resources (e.g., a policy or administrator) to exist, ensure those dependencies are created first.

Test creation with a duplicate or conflicting policy change log scenario (e.g., an identical change to the same field at the same time). The system should enforce appropriate uniqueness or conflict handling rules, returning an error if duplicates are not allowed.
Attempt to create a policy change log with missing or invalid input fields (such as missing namespace or improper date formats). System should return validation errors indicating why creation failed.

Test admin ability to update a non-immutable field of an existing policy change log, like the change_reason or new_value. First, create a policy change log entry, then update it, and verify the changes are reflected. Ensure audit fields remain accurate and immutable fields are not altered.

dependencies.purpose: Create the policy change log to have a valid ID for updating.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update immutable audit fields such as actor_admin_id or created_at. The system should reject the request and return an appropriate error, maintaining data integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy change log record to test immutability on update.

scenario.draft: Try updating a policy change log using a non-existent policyChangeLogId. Confirm that the system returns a 404 not found error, ensuring appropriate error handling for missing resources.

Verify that an admin can soft-delete a policy change log record by its policyChangeLogId. After deletion, attempting to retrieve the same record should result in not found. Begin by creating a policy change log, then delete it, then attempt retrieval.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy change log entry to ensure there is a record available for deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a policy change log with a non-existent or already deleted policyChangeLogId. The system should respond with a not found error, proving robustness against invalid deletions.

Test that a moderator can search and retrieve a paginated, filtered list of post metrics using complex filters—such as view count ranges, activity date, or post reference. Ensure results are accurate and pagination metadata is returned. If necessary, create posts and trigger metrics beforehand to test realistic scenarios.
Submit invalid or malformed filter criteria as a moderator (e.g., non-numeric count range, illogical dates) and confirm the system returns descriptive validation errors.

Execute a search with valid filters as a moderator that yield no matching post metrics (such as filtering by a post ID that does not exist or has no views). The system should handle this gracefully and return an empty result set with appropriate pagination data.

Test retrieving full details of a specific user sanction record as a moderator. This scenario covers the ability of a moderator to access all legal, timeline, and audit data for a sanction record in the system. It requires an existing user sanction to be present, which should be created by an admin or moderator beforehand. Validation includes: successful retrieval for an existing record and proper structure/content of returned data (including member linkage, type, timing, and rationale). Edge cases include forbidden access if the user is not authorized and not found error if an invalid or deleted userSanctionId is provided.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new user sanction record so a moderator can later retrieve its details for review.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new user sanction record by an admin. This scenario requires that a target member exists first in the system. The test must verify that the unique active sanction constraint is enforced (e.g., no duplicate active sanctions for the same user/type). On creation, all input fields must be validated and the full sanction record returned, including member linkage, type, level, status, and rationale. Post-creation, a notification/event is expected per business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Search for or create a valid member account who will be sanctioned for the scenario.

scenario.draft: Test failure case when attempting to create a duplicate active sanction of the same type for the same user. This scenario validates the system constraint that prevents admin or moderator from adding a new sanction if an active one already exists for that user and sanction type. The test creates the initial sanction, then attempts a second with the same user/type, expecting a conflict or validation error response.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure the target member account exists.
Create the first active sanction to set up the conflict for the duplicate creation test.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a user sanction record by a moderator. The moderator must have proper authorization to perform this action, and the target user (member) must exist. The scenario verifies that upon creation, the sanction is added, business rules are respected (including uniqueness constraints), and the correct record is returned. Notification or compliance side effects should also be confirmed.

dependencies.purpose: Find or create a member account to be sanctioned by moderator in test.

scenario.draft: Test the successful update of an existing user sanction record by an admin. The admin should be able to change status, notes, term, or other mutable fields. The test must set up an existing sanction, then update fields such as status or add justification, and validate that audit fields and versioning are correct. The update must only succeed for non-expired/non-deleted records, and failure must be tested for attempts to update a deleted or non-existing sanction.

dependencies.purpose: Create a user sanction that can be updated in this test.

scenario.draft: Test the successful update of a user sanction record by a moderator. Valid disciplines for update include changing the sanction's status, notes, or level after further review or appeal. The test ensures that the moderator has sufficient rights, that audit changes reflect the update, and that business logic allows the update only for non-expired and active records. Attempting updates on missing/deleted records should result in a clear error. The scenario also includes updating only allowed fields and rejecting edits to immutable or forbidden fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create the sanction record as context so the moderator may update it as part of this test.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new daily statistics record for a specific UTC date by an admin. The admin provides a complete payload including all required metric fields and a unique date_utc. On success, the system should return the new record with all fields populated, and subsequent searches should show the added record. This scenario verifies the happy path for OLAP backfilling or analytics corrections.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account to obtain credentials for creating the daily statistics record.

scenario.draft: Test failure when attempting to create a daily statistics record with a date_utc that already exists. First, create a record for a particular date. Then, attempt to create another record using the same date, expecting the system to return a conflict error. This tests the enforcement of the unique-per-day constraint for aggregate statistics records.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account with permission to create daily statistics records.
Create the initial daily statistics record for a specific date to set up the conflict condition.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of all metrics in an existing daily statistics record by an admin user. Initial setup: create a daily statistics record. Then, update all or some fields for that day's stats using the same dailyStatsId. The system should reflect the updates and return the revised record. Non-updatable fields (like date_utc if immutable) are left unchanged. This scenario validates the normal admin analytics correction workflow.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account to allow update operations.
Create the original daily statistics record to allow for later update.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when attempting to update a daily statistics record using a non-existent or deleted dailyStatsId. Expect a 'not found' error response and audit logging of the failed attempt. This validates proper handling of invalid update targets by the analytics management interface.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account to perform the update operation.

scenario.draft: Test successful, permanent deletion of a daily statistics record by an admin. First create a daily statistics record, then delete it using the unique dailyStatsId. The record should be irreversibly removed and subsequent get/list operations for that dailyStatsId should return a not-found error. This scenario checks for irreversible removal and audit logging.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for permission to perform delete operations.
Create the daily statistics record to set up data for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test error response when an admin tries to delete a non-existent or already deleted daily statistics record using an invalid dailyStatsId. The API should return a clear not-found error, and the attempt should appear in the audit logs for compliance review.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account to permit delete attempts.

scenario.draft: Test successful guest login for an anonymous visitor. Provide device and network data (user agent, ip) and check that a JWT token is returned. The system should record a new guest session in the tracking database. This scenario ensures anonymous access, token issuance, and audit logging for guest sessions.

Test error handling when required guest device/auth info is missing or malformed in login request. For example, omit user agent or ip address in the payload and verify that the system returns a validation error. This tests input validation and error feedback for guest authentication.

Test successful logout of a guest session by providing a valid JWT guest token. The system should invalidate the session token, log the event for audit, and return a confirmation response. Attempting to use the token for further guest APIs should fail after logout. This scenario covers session end flow for guest users.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid guest session and token prior to logout.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when attempting to log out as a guest without presenting a valid guest JWT (e.g., no Authorization header or expired/invalid token). The API should return an authentication error and audit the failed attempt. This verifies proper enforcement of guest session protection on logout.

Update the metadata of an existing guest session record with valid data. The test should first ensure a guest record exists (create a new guest session for setup). Then, update fields such as IP address or user agent, verifying that audit fields (such as updated_at) are modified as expected and that the returned record reflects the new values. Only admins are permitted to perform this action.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guest session to obtain a valid guestId before updating metadata.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a guest session record using a non-existent or already soft-deleted guestId. The API should return a not found error. This scenario ensures proper error handling for invalid resource references.

Attempt to update a guest session record with a user who lacks admin privileges. The API should return an error indicating insufficient permissions. This validates role-based access control and enforcement.

Soft-delete an existing guest session record by guestId and verify that the record is no longer available in subsequent queries. Ensure audit fields (deleted_at) are appropriately set. Only admins are authorized. The test should create a guest session record, then soft-delete it, then attempt to retrieve it and confirm it is not found.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guest session record to obtain a guestId before testing soft-deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to soft-delete a guest session using a non-existent or already deleted guestId and confirm that the API returns a not found error. This scenario validates proper error handling.
Attempt to soft-delete a guest session record with a non-admin user. The API must return a permission denied error. This scenario ensures enforcement of admin-only delete operations.

Retrieve a paginated, filtered list of members using basic filter criteria such as email or nickname substring. Confirm that results only include members matching the search criteria and that pagination metadata is correct. Only admin and moderator roles are allowed to access the full list.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure an admin account exists and is authenticated to test admin search.
Register one or more member users to ensure there are searchable records.

scenario.draft: Perform a search for members using a filter that should result in zero matches (e.g., a non-existent email or nickname). Confirm that the API returns an empty result set and valid pagination information.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure an admin account is available to perform the search.

scenario.draft: Attempt to search for members using an account without admin or moderator privileges. Ensure the API refuses access and returns a suitable error message, validating access control enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account to use for the unauthorized attempt.

scenario.draft: Perform a member search as an authenticated moderator using email, nickname, status, or registration date as filters. Verify that returned results respect filter criteria and pagination. Confirm that sensitive fields remain unexposed and that the operation succeeds for moderator role.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as a moderator.
Register member users to be listed.

scenario.draft: Attempt to access the member search endpoint as a user without moderator privilege. The API should return a permission denied error, validating security controls.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member user to use for the unauthorized attempt.

scenario.draft: Retrieve detailed profile information for a valid memberId as an admin. Confirm that all profile fields are included except sensitive hashes (e.g., password). Validate that audit and status fields align with the member's lifecycle.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin to permit profile detail retrieval.
Register a new member to obtain a valid memberId for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve a member profile using a non-existent or deleted memberId. Ensure the API returns a not found error, validating error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to perform the detail lookup.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve member profile details using an account without sufficient privileges (e.g., a regular member user). Ensure the API blocks access and returns an appropriate permission denied error.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member user to use for the unauthorized attempt.

scenario.draft: Test creating a new policy document with all required and several optional fields. Confirm that the document is stored correctly, version is set, and audit fields are populated. The scenario should include using an admin-authenticated session, setting a unique title and version, and validating that the resulting document is immediately available via the appropriate detail-retrieval endpoint. The test checks the integration with the compliance workflow and confirms correct status is saved.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin and retrieve credentials for authorization before creating the document.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a new policy document using a title and version that already exist in the system. The test should first create a baseline policy document, then attempt to submit another with the same title and version, expecting a conflict or validation error. This ensures unique constraints on policy documents are enforced, as per business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure admin is registered and authenticated.
Create the initial policy document with specific title and version to set up the conflict condition.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing policy document with new text, updated title or version, and status changes. The test should first create a policy document as an admin, retrieve its ID, and then submit an update with valid modifications. The success criteria are that the updated fields are reflected in the response, audit logs are updated, and version history is maintained if applicable.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for the session and authorization.
Create an initial policy document to obtain a valid policyDocumentId for update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a policy document using a non-existent or already-deleted policyDocumentId. The test should submit an update request with a fabricated UUID, expecting a 404 or appropriate not-found error, which validates the system's error handling for invalid document references.

dependencies.purpose: Register/admin login for necessary credentials.

scenario.draft: Test the soft-deletion of an existing policy document by a valid admin. The test creates a policy document, deletes it, and then attempts to fetch it, expecting a not-found result. The test ensures the soft-delete logic applies (deleted_at is set) and the record is excluded from ordinary queries but retained for audit.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for authentication.
Create the policy document to obtain a valid policyDocumentId for deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a policy document using a random or already-deleted policyDocumentId. Confirm that the system returns a not-found error and that compliance/audit logs are consistent for the attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin session for authentication before attempting deletion.

scenario.draft: Perform a search on guest session records with filters that match no existing entries (e.g., bogus IP or session token). The test should confirm zero results are returned, proper pagination metadata is included in the response, and the audit log reflects the search attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to ensure proper search authorization.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a specific guest tracking record by guestId. First, create several guest sessions, extract a valid guestId, and then request its detail as an admin. The test validates that all expected fields (session token, IP, user agent, timestamps) are returned accurately, and that authorization checks work. Also, attempt unauthorized access with non-admin credentials to verify access control.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to enable lookup of guest records.
Generate at least one guest session to obtain a real guestId for detail lookup.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve guest tracking details using an invalid or already-deleted guestId. The test expects a not-found error and verifies that the error message and code are consistent with compliance requirements. Attempts with a random UUID must not return private data or succeed.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to perform access to guest tracking records.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the full detail of a specific outgoing email log as an admin. First, create a new outgoing email log record using the creation endpoint, capture the returned emailLogId, and then fetch the details using GET. Validate that all fields match those set during creation and that all communication and audit metadata are accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Create an email log and return its unique emailLogId to use in the retrieval test.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when trying to fetch a non-existent or already soft-deleted email log by ID. Use a fabricated or recently deleted emailLogId to trigger a 404 error and validate the system response.

dependencies.purpose: Soft-delete a valid email log record and use its ID to confirm that fetching returns a not found error.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new outgoing email log by an admin. Provide all required metadata—such as recipient, email type, sent status, and provider details—and verify that the created log record contains all fields set correctly, and is included in subsequent search results. Confirm audit logging and data integrity.

Test error handling when attempting to create a duplicate outgoing email log, especially if an idempotency constraint exists. Submit the same creation payload twice and ensure the system returns a conflict or duplicate error for the second attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial email log with a unique identifier and metadata to establish the condition for a duplicate error scenario.

scenario.draft: Test updating fields of an existing outgoing email log as an admin (e.g., correcting the recipient, updating status, or changing provider response). First, create a log, then perform a PUT to update certain metadata, and verify that fields are changed correctly and version/audit fields are updated. Confirm that all business and schema validation rules are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create an outgoing email log to provide an emailLogId and baseline data for update testing.

scenario.draft: Test updating a non-existent or already soft-deleted email log. Attempt to PUT with a fabricated or deleted emailLogId and confirm that the response is a proper not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Soft-delete an actual email log and attempt to update it to trigger an error response.

scenario.draft: Test the soft deletion of an outgoing email log record as an admin. First, create a new email log, confirm it is retrievable, then delete it and verify it is no longer found in detail or search queries, but that historical/audit links still exist where appropriate.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new outgoing email log record to obtain a valid emailLogId for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to soft-delete a non-existent or already deleted email log. Use an invalid or previously deleted emailLogId and assert that the system correctly returns a not found error response.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure an email log is deleted, then use its ID to reattempt deletion, simulating a double-delete scenario.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a filtered and paginated list of ad integration logs as an admin. Populate test logs via the creation endpoint, then search with filters (e.g., by event type, status, or date range), and validate that the returned log entries match requested search criteria and pagination works as intended.

dependencies.purpose: Create sample ad integration logs to ensure relevant data exists for search and pagination tests.

scenario.draft: Test searching ad integration logs with filters that guarantee no matches (e.g., using an improbable event type or date range). Validate that the response is an empty result set and ensure no errors occur due to the empty search.
